title: KMS alert thresholds tuning notes (SRE/Observability)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- During initial rollout of KMS wrapper + instrumentation, KMS dependency alerts were too noisy (esp. us-east + staging), causing unnecessary paging.
- We need a consistent, evidence-friendly set of SLOs and alert thresholds for KMS dependency health, with environment/region splits and a clear rollout plan.
- Primary goal: catch real KMS degradation that will cause customer impact (decrypt/envelope failures or elevated 5xx), while reducing false positives caused by low traffic, batch jobs, or expected transient throttling.

Scope
- Metrics/alerts for KMS calls made by Redwood services (control plane + data plane).
- Alert thresholds for: latency, error rate by canonical taxonomy, throttling/backpressure, circuit breaker open, and healthcheck failures.
- Includes rollout plan for paging policy and evaluation criteria.

Assumptions
- KMS client wrapper emits standardized metrics + tags (per ENG-4822 and PR-18434 / PR-18515). We rely on:
  - kms.request.latency_ms (histogram)
  - kms.request.count (counter)
  - kms.request.errors (counter) tagged by error_category and provider_error_code
  - kms.circuit_breaker.state (gauge or event) / kms.circuit_breaker.open.count
  - kms.throttle_budget.exhausted.count (from PR-18570)
  - kms.healthcheck.status (0/1) for internal health endpoint (PR-18527)
- Error taxonomy categories (canonical): AccessDenied, NotFound, Throttling, Timeout, InvalidCiphertext, DependencyUnavailable, Unknown.
- Metric dimensions to standardize (avoid cardinality blowups):
  - env: prod|staging|dev
  - region: us-east-1|us-west-2|eu-west-1|...
  - deployment_mode: hosted|dedicated|private
  - service: (bounded list; no instance-id)
  - operation: decrypt|encrypt|generate_data_key|describe_key|...
  - error_category: (bounded list)

Proposed SLOs (internal, dependency-focused)
NOTE: These are not customer-facing SLAs. They are used to set alerting/paging and to reason about reliability risk.

1) KMS request success SLO (decrypt path) — prod
- Objective: >= 99.95% success over 30 days for decrypt-related operations.
- Success definition: non-error outcome OR handled transient outcomes that do not cause request failure (e.g., throttling that is retried successfully within budget).
- Error budget: 0.05% failures. We page on burn-rate, not on 30d only.

2) KMS request latency SLO (decrypt path) — prod
- Objective: p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 750ms (per service/region) for decrypt.
- Rationale: decrypt in hot path can cascade into tail latency / retries; p99 is the early warning.
- Caveat: workloads differ by region; we treat latency as a symptom, page only when correlated with error/burn or when healthcheck fails.

3) KMS throttling tolerance (soft SLO) — prod
- Not a strict SLO; used for early warning and capacity planning.
- Goal: throttling events < 0.1% of KMS calls (5m window) sustained, and no throttle budget exhaustion in steady state.

Environment-specific notes
- Staging/dev are inherently spiky; alerts should not page on-call unless they predict prod blast radius (e.g., shared KMS project/account, or wrapper regression being rolled out).

Alert philosophy (what pages vs what tickets)
Pager triggers should correspond to one of:
A) customer impact already happening (decrypt failures / elevated 5xx)
B) extremely likely imminent impact (circuit breaker open, healthcheck failing across fleet)
C) a rapid burn of error budget (burn-rate) that indicates sustained degradation
Everything else should be a ticket with links to dashboards and suggested mitigations.

Key alerts (proposed)

1) KMS decrypt failure rate (pager)
Signal
- Error rate for operation=decrypt (and generate_data_key if in same hot path) where error_category in [Timeout, DependencyUnavailable, InvalidCiphertext, Unknown] OR where wrapper marks final failure after retries.
Thresholds (prod)
- Page if error_rate >= 0.5% for 5m AND request_count >= 500 (per region/service) OR global request_count >= 2000.
- Page if error_rate >= 0.2% for 15m AND request_count >= 2,000.
- Also page on high burn-rate relative to 30d SLO: 14x for 5m or 6x for 30m (implementation depends on tooling).
Why this should reduce false positives
- Adds request_count gating (previously paging in low-traffic regions on 2–3 errors).
- Filters out AccessDenied/NotFound as separate actionable alerts (often config changes, not dependency outage).

2) KMS circuit breaker open (pager)
Signal
- kms.circuit_breaker.state=open sustained.
Thresholds
- Page if >= 10% of instances for a prod service in a region have breaker open for >= 3m.
- Page immediately if breaker open across >= 2 regions for the same tier.
Notes
- This is intended as “stop the bleeding” indicator. Pair with runbook steps to reduce load and/or fail over.

3) KMS healthcheck failing (pager)
Signal
- kms.healthcheck.status=0 (internal endpoint) aggregated by service/region.
Thresholds
- Page if healthcheck failing in prod for >= 5m AND affects >= 2 AZs (or >= 25% of pods) for a service.
- Ticket if failing in staging only.

4) KMS throttling early warning (ticket -> page if severe)
Signal
- error_category=Throttling rate + throttle budget exhaustion.
Thresholds
- Ticket if throttling_rate >= 1% for 10m (prod) AND request_count >= 1,000.
- Page if throttle_budget.exhausted.count > 0 for 5m AND correlated with elevated decrypt failures or latency p99 > 1.5s.
Rationale
- Throttling alone may be handled by retry/backoff; it becomes urgent when it starts causing final failures or breaker opens.

5) KMS latency anomaly (ticket)
Signal
- p99 latency for decrypt.
Thresholds
- Ticket if p99 > 1.5s for 15m (prod) AND request_count >= 2,000.
- Escalate to page only if combined with: error_rate >= 0.2% (same window) OR circuit breaker open.
Rationale
- Latency alerts were the #1 noise source. Treat as symptom unless it crosses into error budget burn.

6) AccessDenied / permission issues (ticket, targeted routing)
Signal
- error_category=AccessDenied.
Thresholds
- Ticket if AccessDenied > 0 in prod for any service (since typically misconfig) but route to owning team (Platform/Private Deployments) not on-call page.
- Page only if AccessDenied spikes > 50/min for 5m AND causing elevated customer-facing errors (depends on mapping; see runbook).
Notes
- Common causes: wrong principal, missing kms:Decrypt permission, key policy mis-scope, wrong key ARN/region.
- For Private: these may be customer config issues; ensure error messages are actionable (PR-18486) and support playbook references exist.

False positives observed (what we’re fixing)
1) Low-traffic regions
- Symptom: a single timeout in a region with <100 requests/5m triggered a high error_rate.
- Fix: request_count gating + global aggregation option for page.

2) Staging churn
- Symptom: CI / load tests create bursty p99 spikes; paging thresholds matched prod.
- Fix: no paging in staging; only tickets, and only when used as canary for prod rollout.

3) Throttling that self-resolves
- Symptom: transient Throttling leading to alerts even though wrapper retries succeeded.
- Fix: alert on “final failure” (after retry budget) + throttle budget exhaustion as escalation.

4) Metric dimension/cardinality drift
- Symptom: dashboards/alerts split by high-cardinality tags (key_arn, customer_id) leading to unreliable monitors.
- Fix: enforce tag allowlist; key identifiers only in logs/audit events, not in metric tags.

Dashboards/panels to standardize (from observability-pack PR-844)
- Overview
  - KMS success rate (final outcomes)
  - Error rate by error_category
  - Throttling rate + throttle budget exhaustion
  - Latency p50/p95/p99
  - Circuit breaker open rate
- Drilldowns
  - by env/region/service
  - by operation
- Correlations
  - request 5xx rate for dependent services overlaid with KMS errors
  - deploy markers (wrapper version rollout)

Rollout plan for paging changes
Phase 0 — Preconditions (done / in-flight)
- Metric namespacing agreed (see Slack 1747409983).
- Dashboards shipped (PR-844) and verified in staging.
- Runbook updated with new fields/queries (kms-decrypt-failures-runbook).

Phase 1 — Shadow alerts (1 week)
- Create new monitors with proposed thresholds but set to “no page” / notify-only in #eng-sre-alerts.
- Compare to existing monitors; track: pages prevented, true positives missed, time-to-detect.
- Add a simple weekly summary:
  - count of alerts
  - count correlated with customer-facing errors
  - top regions/services generating noise

Phase 2 — Prod paging with guardrails (2 weeks)
- Enable paging only for:
  - decrypt failure rate (pager)
  - circuit breaker open (pager)
  - healthcheck failing (pager)
- Keep latency and throttling as tickets during this phase.
- Add explicit auto-silence rules during known maintenance windows / game day.

Phase 3 — Mature burn-rate alerting (post-game day)
- Move primary paging criteria to burn-rate monitors (where supported), keep static thresholds as backup.
- Enable throttling escalation paging only if we see repeated incidents where throttling preceded outage.

Success criteria (what “good” looks like)
- Reduce KMS-related pages by >= 60% week-over-week without increasing MTTR.
- Zero missed incidents where decrypt final failure rate exceeded 0.5% for >10m in prod.
- Clear ownership routing for AccessDenied/NotFound alerts (Platform vs Private Deployments vs Support).
- On-call feedback: alerts are actionable and map to specific mitigations.

Open questions / TODO
- Do we want separate thresholds for Hosted vs Private? (Private customers may run in constrained KMS quotas.) Tentative: same baseline thresholds, but allow per-tenant override at install-time while keeping prod paging thresholds fixed for Redwood-owned environments.
- Confirm request_count gating values with real traffic baselines per region (need 2 weeks of data post-wrapper rollout).
- Decide whether to include describe_key latency/errors in paging (currently no; could matter during rotation workflows).
- Validate that “final failure” is correctly marked by wrapper across all languages/services.

Notes from incident/noise threads (summary)
- 1746280021: Most noise came from latency p99 spikes without corresponding errors; decision was to demote latency to ticket unless correlated.
- us-east timeout spike incident showed retry amplification risk; follow-up in hotfix PR reduced storm behavior (reference in incident thread; see also retry budget guardrails).

Last updated checklist
- [x] Added request_count gating
- [x] Split by env; removed staging paging
- [x] Added breaker + healthcheck pager signals
- [ ] Validate throttle budget metrics in prod
- [ ] After 2 weeks, revisit thresholds with observed distributions (p99 and error rate)
